## Calculated Values {#sec-calculated}

Parameters derived from mathematical formulas and economic models.

### Bad Policy Costs Total (US): $5.03T {#sec-bad_policy_cost_total_us}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total annual US bad policy costs (Tier 1 + Tier 2 with overlap discount). Bottom-up empirical estimate based on specific, measurable policy failures. More defensible than theoretical decomposition because each component is verifiable.

**Inputs**:

- [Bad Policy Costs (Tier 1)](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_tier1_total) 🔢: $3.92T
- [Bad Policy Costs (Tier 2)](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_tier2_total) 🔢: $2T
- [Overlap Discount Factor](#sec-bad_policy_us_overlap_discount): 0.85:1

$$
\begin{gathered}
C_{bad,total} \\
= BadUS \times (C_{tier1} + C_{tier2}) \\
= 0.85 \times (\$3.92T + \$2T) \\
= \$5.03T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } C_{tier1} \\
= C_{tax} + C_{wars} + C_{drugs} + C_{tariffs} \\
+ C_{ff,explicit} + C_{healthcare} + C_{housing} \\
+ C_{ag} \\
= \$546B + \$400B + \$90B + \$160B + \$50B + \$1.2T \\
+ \$1.4T + \$75B \\
= \$3.92T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } C_{tier2} \\
= C_{ff,external} + C_{licensing} + C_{migration} \\
+ C_{defense} + C_{prison} + C_{infra} \\
= \$600B + \$200B + \$500B + \$400B + \$150B + \$150B \\
= \$2T
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/optimocracy-paper#bad-policy-costs](../appendix/optimocracy-paper#bad-policy-costs)

*? Low confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

$$
\begin{gathered}

\text{where } C_{bad,total} \\
= BadUS \times (C_{tier1} + C_{tier2}) \\

= \$5.03T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } C_{tier1} \\
= C_{tax} + C_{wars} + C_{drugs} + C_{tariffs} \\
+ C_{ff,explicit} + C_{healthcare} + C_{housing} \\
+ C_{ag} \\
= \$546B + \$400B + \$90B + \$160B + \$50B + \$1.2T \\
+ \$1.4T + \$75B \\
= \$3.92T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } C_{tier2} \\
= C_{ff,external} + C_{licensing} + C_{migration} \\
+ C_{defense} + C_{prison} + C_{infra} \\
= \$600B + \$200B + \$500B + \$400B + \$150B + \$150B \\
= \$2T
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/optimocracy-paper#bad-policy-costs](../appendix/optimocracy-paper#bad-policy-costs)

### Bad Policy Costs (Tier 1): $3.92T {#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_tier1_total}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Sum of Tier 1 (well-documented) bad policy costs: tax compliance + failed wars + drug war + tariffs + fossil fuel explicit + healthcare inefficiency + housing/zoning + agricultural subsidies. These have strong empirical backing and high economist consensus.

**Inputs**:

- [Tax Compliance Cost](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_tax_compliance) 📊: $546B (95% CI: $450B - $650B)
- [Failed Wars (Amortized)](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_failed_wars) 📊: $400B (95% CI: $300B - $600B)
- [Drug War Cost](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_drug_war) 📊: $90B (95% CI: $60B - $150B)
- [Tariff Cost (GDP Loss)](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_tariffs) 📊: $160B (95% CI: $90B - $250B)
- [Fossil Fuel Explicit Subsidies](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_fossil_fuel_explicit) 📊: $50B (95% CI: $30B - $80B)
- [Healthcare System Inefficiency](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_healthcare_inefficiency) 📊: $1.20T (95% CI: $1T - $1.50T)
- [Housing/Zoning Restrictions Cost](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_housing_zoning) 📊: $1.40T (95% CI: $1T - $2T)
- [Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss](#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_agricultural_subsidies) 📊: $75B (95% CI: $50B - $120B)

$$
\begin{gathered}
C_{tier1} \\
= C_{tax} + C_{wars} + C_{drugs} + C_{tariffs} \\
+ C_{ff,explicit} + C_{healthcare} + C_{housing} + C_{ag} \\
= \$546B + \$400B + \$90B + \$160B + \$50B + \$1.2T + \$1.4T \\
+ \$75B \\

## External Data Sources {#sec-external}

### Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss: $75B {#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_agricultural_subsidies}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Deadweight loss from US agricultural subsidies. Direct subsidies ~$30B/yr but create larger distortions: overproduction, environmental damage, benefits concentrated in large farms (top 10% receive 78% of subsidies). Total welfare loss ~$75B. Textbook example of capture - very high economist consensus.

**Source**: [@ewg-farm-subsidies]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$50B, $120B] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $25B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $50B and $120B (±47%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-bad_policy_cost_us_agricultural_subsidies.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Defense Above Deterrence: $400B {#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_defense_above_deterrence}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US defense spending above deterrence requirements. US spends ~$900B/yr on defense; many defense economists (Posen, Preble, etc.) argue $400-500B achieves equivalent deterrence given geography, nuclear arsenal, and alliance structure. Excess ~$400B/yr funds force projection, not homeland defense.

**Source**: [@posen2014]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$250B, $600B] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $120B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $250B and $600B (±44%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-bad_policy_cost_us_defense_above_deterrence.qmd >}}

*~ Medium confidence*

:::

### Healthcare System Inefficiency: $1.20T {#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_healthcare_inefficiency}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US healthcare spending inefficiency. US spends ~$4.5T/yr (18% GDP) vs 9-11% in comparable OECD countries with similar/better outcomes. Papanicolas et al. (2018 JAMA) and multiple studies document $1-1.5T in excess spending from administrative complexity, high prices, and poor care coordination. Very high economist consensus.

**Source**: [@papanicolas2018]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$1T, $1.50T] • Distribution: Normal (SE: $150B)

**What this means**: This estimate has moderate uncertainty. The true value likely falls between $1T and $1.50T (±21%). This represents a reasonable range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-bad_policy_cost_us_healthcare_inefficiency.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Housing/Zoning Restrictions Cost: $1.40T {#sec-bad_policy_cost_us_housing_zoning}

GDP loss from housing/zoning restrictions. Annual cost ~$1.4T. Very high economist consensus across political spectrum.

## Core Definitions {#sec-definitions}

Fundamental parameters and constants used throughout the analysis.

### Overlap Discount Factor: 0.85:1 {#sec-bad_policy_us_overlap_discount}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Discount factor to account for overlap between bad policy cost categories. Fossil fuel externalities partially overlap with climate/health costs counted elsewhere. Migration restrictions partially captured in labor market inefficiencies.

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*Core definition*

:::

```{=html}
<script>
// Conservative lazy loading: only load images actually in viewport
(function() {
  'use strict';
  
  let imageObserver = null;
  let loadTimeout = null;
  
  function enableLazyLoading() {
    const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
    
    // Use Intersection Observer with conservative threshold
    // rootMargin: '50px' means only load images within 50px of viewport
    // This prevents loading images passed through during hash navigation
    imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio > 0) {
          const img = entry.target;
          // Only load if image is actually visible (not just passed through)
          if (img.dataset.src) {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.removeAttribute('data-src');
          } else if (!img.hasAttribute('loading')) {
            // For images without data-src, use native lazy loading
            img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          }
          observer.unobserve(img);
        }
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: '50px',  // Only load images within 50px of viewport
      threshold: 0.01      // Trigger when at least 1% visible
    });
    
    images.forEach(img => {
      imageObserver.observe(img);
    });
  }
  
  // Handle hash navigation (clicking links to sections)
  // Delay loading to avoid loading images passed through during jump
  function handleHashNavigation() {
    if (loadTimeout) clearTimeout(loadTimeout);
    // Wait 300ms after navigation to let scroll settle
    // Images will load naturally via Intersection Observer when visible
    loadTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      // Scroll has settled, Intersection Observer will handle visible images
      // No action needed - observer is already watching
    }, 300);
  }
  
  // Initialize on page load
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enableLazyLoading);
  } else {
    enableLazyLoading();
  }
  
  // Handle hash changes (clicking anchor links)
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', handleHashNavigation);
  
  // Also handle initial hash if page loads with one
  if (window.location.hash) {
    setTimeout(handleHashNavigation, 100);
  }
})();
</script>
```
